title: 17 weeks of making game with Claude Opus in Godot
author: RUSuper
selftext:
Hello guys again :)

It's Sunday so here is the newest weekly update (Even though it usually goes on Mondays I am left without usage so it comes 1 day early this week). Thanks again to everyone who downloaded the demo and left feedback ☺️

[**DEMO LINK DOWNLOAD - FREE**](https://profactor.itch.io/nightshoal)

**I want to say one thing about video for this week right away**. A lot of things in this video are in the rough shape, docking sites has mesh collisions, every tree is a placeholder (models are already done via TripoAI so they will come up next week). A lot of fixes is needed so please do not mind things like houses not being perfectly positioned and quality dropping from previous weeks, I will try to fix them all by next week.

This week was all about zone 2, the bay under the big bridge (I call it **Crown Bay** for now). Last week it was just two harbours you couldn't even sail to, and this week the whole bay got built from the plan, so you can sail there, fish, explore, do jobs for the people there and dock at its landings. It's still behind a switch so it's not in the demo, it comes with the full release.

If you see this for the first time, Nightshoal is a fishing and exploration game set in the 1920s. You have one boat and you fish with it, but you also explore small islands and collect ships in bottles, and at night it gets dangerous (still cozy style, mostly pirates and the inconvenience of not seeing anything). I'm making it with AI tools (mainly **Opus 5.5**) and every week I write what I used and how.

**What was done this week:**

Zone 2 can be sailed now. You sail south from home or come in from the black market (In between zone for Zone 1 and Zone 2), and you enter the bay under the bridge. The bay has its own land and trees (birch groves, wind-bent cypress on the coast, street trees in town), fog in the mornings with a fog bell (fog might need a little bit of work tbh), and the bridge city loads in pieces so it doesn't kill the frame rate.

There are 22 new fish in the bay, each with its own images, and they pay a bit more (x1.25) like last week's plan said.

The bay got its story chapter, 26 side jobs for the people in the city and six working boats with skippers out on the water...

The city yard sells the bay gear: basically new lamps, engines, the Fog Glass that sees through the fog, a hand winch for the deep pools and a new hull, the Trader.

Exploring... there are 20 places with real rewards, a surveyors trail where you collect tags, 11 sights, 21 rumours you hear from people and notes on the chart.

At sea there are four pirates (they stay out of the city water as I felt it is unrealistic for pirates to come close to a big city), a customs launch that searches you for the cook crate, a fisheries patrol at night and cargo steamers on their lane. There are also six sea events which are similar in nature to zone 1 events :) Pelicans dive on schools of fish too just a small detail I wanted heh.

Every place in the bay has its own small sounds at its own hours, like traffic on the bridge, trams, the cannery's whistle at every shift change, sea lions on Seal Rocks and the fog bell. Each of the 17 people also got a murmur when you open their page.

There are 6 new ships in bottles, 54 new awards and 21 curios for the Cabinet (12 you find and 9 people give you). The Cabinet had no room left for them, so I picked a collector's drawer that slides out of the counter, and I have no idea how I will make it in the future... Maybe just "page" settup.

The two landings (Toll House Landing under the bridge and the Pilot Station on the sand hook) were first built from zone 1 harbour sets with a few houses swapped, and I didn't like that at all lol. So they got rebuilt from the bay own pieces, and now the docking view is literally the same game world seen from a camera on the dock, so the place looks exactly like when you sail past it (which was always the way it worked in zone 1 anyway).

The bay got its own boats and birds too heh. The islands look got a big pass (more in workflow), and my in-game editor now works in zone 2 too with a free camera, so I can move things around myself.

**Workflow:**

This week I let several agents work at the same time as long as they don't touch the same files (max 2 game windows at once, last time 4 of them froze my Mac...). **Jev** still picks the effort level for every task.

The look of the bay islands went through the **Gauntlet loop** again, but with what I learned last week. First the game took screenshots of 4 places (Fog Bell, the quarry, the old engine works and the quarantine island) by day and by night, and **OpenAI (image API)** painted the mockups over those exact screenshots, so nothing ends up in a different place than in the game. Then every round a fresh critic compares the game with the mockup blind, and if a place wins twice it's done. After 7 rounds 3 of the 4 nights beat their mockups. The days still lose, mostly because every island had the same flat shape with the same cliff around it, and that's being rebuilt now.

New rule this week: if a model fails 5 times it goes to **Tripo**. Opus builds it in **Blender** first and a critic checks it against a sheet with 4 views (front, right, back and left, made with **OpenAI (image API)**). After 5 losses I get the sheet and make the model in **Tripo** myself. **Tripo** got bunch of models this way... The first sheets I got were split badly (the views were cutting into each other) so **Opus** wrote a smarter splitter, and I always forget if **Tripo** should export triangles or quads xD (it works either way, they get converted, but yeah).

The whole test suite runs now before anything lands (634 test files and as I get more and more it takes more time :/ ). Bug of the week...was a tutorial test that failed only when about 30 other tests ran before it, because one of them fished up a piece of junk (a pocket watch) and its card stayed open lol.

**What was used this week:**

**Opus 5.5 (Claude Code)** did basically all of the building: zone 2 land, jobs, events, the landings, the boats, the islands look, models in **Blender** (headless and through MCP) and everything in **Godot**. It also filmed and cut the trailer.

**Tripo** made bunch of models from the sheets after Opus tries failed. Last week 12 harbour people were made in **Tripo** too.

**Jev** picked the effort level of every task and made the calls I didn't make myself.

**OpenAI (image API)** made the mockups of the bay places, the 4 view sheets for **Tripo**, the paintings of the 22 new fish and the cards for the new curios.

**ElevenLabs** made the bay's sounds and the people's murmurs.

**Godot** is still the engine.

**Total cost:**

CHECK: same as last week unless something changed

**Claude Max** 200$ x 4 = 800$

**Astra** 100$ x 1 = 100$

**ElevenLabs** x 11$ = 11$

**Tripo** 20$ x 3 = 60$

**OpenAI API** credits 80$ = 80$

Other things I forgot about 100$ = 100$ (around)

Around 1100-1150$

That would be it for this week, any feedback is appreciated :)

comments.author: Maksim_Volganin_11
comments.body: The atmosphere here is incredible, especially the transition to night around the suspension bridge! I really liked the mix of top-down sailing and switching to first-person when docking. That moral choice with the four men caught in the net ("room for two") caught my eye too. Did Claude Opus help mostly with the GDScript logic, or did it assist with shaders and water physics as well? Looks super promising!

replies.author: RUSuper
replies.body:
Opus wrote code entirely including shaders and water physics though this is 6th iteration of the water, it evolved from week one several times. This one in particular is final version as is in the game since like week 8 or something. Took a lot of manual exploration on the net of shaders and water movement until I got what I actually liked. Previous water shader was also very nice in my opinion, but performance wise it was heavier than this one and this might be slightly better. 

Yeah moral dilemmas around the sea should impact your game ending depending on your choices during the game, I will see yet how that goes, but so far they are there, choices are recorded in the background (for that 1 of 3 endings that I planned) and in captain journal also and while it doesn't impact future gameplay they do matter in the game in different ways :)
